chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf, from Abu al-Hasan (the first) (peace be upon him) who said:

The daughters of the daughter (granddaughters via daughter) take the place of the daughters if the deceased has no daughters and no other heirs besides them, and the daughters of the son (granddaughters via son) take the place of the son if the deceased has no male offspring and no other heirs besides them.

key_terms.بَنَاتُ الْابْنِ: Daughters of the son (paternal granddaughters via male line)
key_terms.بَنَاتُ الْبِنْتِ: Daughters of the daughter (paternal granddaughters via female line)

ai.seo_question: How do granddaughters inherit in Shia Islamic law when there are no direct children?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *qadam* (standing in place) within the framework of *al-Asl* (the root) and *al-Zawj* (the spouse). It distinguishes between the inheritance of *banat al-bint* (daughters of daughters), who inherit as daughters only in the absence of any other heirs, and *banat al-ibn* (daughters of sons), who assume the position of a son (*ibn*) when there is no male offspring, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise lineage-based distribution.
